58	| `error` | a sentence under the field, `role="alert"`, `aria-invalid` on the field |
59	| `disabled` | both fields and the button locked while a write is in flight |
60	| `loading` | the button says "Posting…"; the card stays on screen, it does not disappear |
61	
62	**The fields have no visible label**, as in the mock-up — two placeholders in a card that is
63	obviously a form. They do carry an `aria-label`: a placeholder on its own is a label that
64	disappears at exactly the moment somebody starts typing.
65	
66	**The placeholder is therefore text under WCAG 1.4.3, not decoration**, and is held to the same
67	4.5:1 floor as everything else ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens). It is the only
68	thing on screen saying what goes in the field.
69	
70	**The focus ring is the screen's, and no component may cancel it.** It is declared once, in
71	`frontend/src/index.css`, on `:focus-visible` inside `@layer base` — and a Tailwind utility on
72	the element (`outline-none`) beats it whatever its specificity, because `@layer utilities` is a
73	**later layer** and layer order settles the cascade before specificity is consulted. A field that
74	wants a different ring says so with a `focus-visible:outline-*` utility, which competes inside
75	the same layer; it never removes the ring and leaves nothing.
76	
77	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — found by measuring the *built* stylesheet,
78	from the trunk, where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is available):
79	
80	- **Strengthen the base rule instead — `!important`, a heavier selector.** Neither reaches it.
81	  The rule matched and lost on one property in a later layer, so no amount of specificity
82	  changes the outcome; the only cure at that level is to move the ring into `@layer utilities`,
83	  which would put the screen's one accessibility guarantee in the layer components write to.
84	- **Assert the ring in `vitest`.** The component suite runs in jsdom, which loads no application
85	  CSS, implements no `@layer`, and does not support `:focus-visible` — a test for the ring's
86	  presence in the *source* would have passed on a screen with no visible ring at all, which is
87	  exactly the state the repository was in. The assertion belongs in a browser: `e2e/ui/`.
88	
89	**An error appears only after the field is left**, never on every character. Telling somebody
90	their signature is too short at the first letter is noise — and noise is what teaches people to
91	ignore red text that means something real.
92	
93	**No field stops accepting input at its bound; the message under it is the bound.** Both fields
94	carried `maxLength` until 2026-09-17 and it was removed on purpose. The HTML attribute counts
95	UTF-16 code units, which nothing else in this system counts, so the signature field stopped
96	accepting characters after 40 emoji rather than 80 — and it stopped *silently*, which is the
97	worst of the three symptoms the bound had: the guest loses what they typed with no sentence
98	anywhere saying why. A validator message a person can read is the whole remedy, and it now
99	counts the same code points the server counts.
100	
101	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — taken outside `/forge:sdd` on GitHub issue
102	#28, so there is no `delta.md` in which to declare it):
103	
104	- **Keep `maxLength` as a generous safety valve (×4).** It would still truncate silently, only
105	  later and at a number matching no rule anywhere. A cap nobody can predict is worse than no cap
106	  for the person meeting it.
107	- **Clamp on paste to the code-point bound.** A visible, correct hard stop — but it is a fourth
108	  place that measures text, it needs a screen state of its own to explain itself, and the
109	  message under the field already says the same thing without any of that.
110	- **Leave it and fix only the validator.** The two would then disagree about the same field: the
111	  message would say 80 while the field accepted 40. That is the defect, not a smaller version
112	  of it.
113	
114	**The button is `disabled` until both fields have content.** The rule lives in
115	`frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/guestbookEntry.ts`; the screen only applies it.
116	
117	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — the two files this document cites moved
118	when the tree was recut by bounded context. The decision itself is
119	[`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Frontend — where a file goes and
120	[`../architecture.md`](../architecture.md) § What a new feature adds; this edit is only its
121	consequence, and it is recorded because the edit was made from the trunk, where no `delta.md`
122	exists to call it editorial):
123	
124	- **Leave the citations pointing at the old paths.** They resolve to nothing, and
125	  `backtick-paths` says so on every pull request. A screen specification pointing at a file
126	  that is not there is precisely the drift between screen and specification this document
127	  exists to prevent — and the rule it points at did not move, only the file did.
128	
129	**The card clears after a successful post and does not clear after a failed one.** The first, so
130	that the next guest does not send somebody else's entry a second time. The second, because a
131	form that empties its fields after an error is a form nobody retries.
132	
133	**After a successful post the screen returns to the unfiltered guestbook, newest first.** An
134	entry sent while searching would land outside the result, and an entry you cannot see looks like
135	an entry that was not saved.
136	
137	### The toolbar (`EntryToolbar`)
138	
139	| State | What is visible |
140	|---|---|
141	| `default` | an empty search field, "Newest" selected |
142	| `searching` | the typed phrase, the result sentence says how many match |
143	| `stale` | the previous answer stays on screen, its sentence carries ` — updating…`, and the live region is `aria-busy` |
144	
145	**Search asks the server, it does not filter an array on screen.** An entry that did not fit in
146	the first piece must be findable — a browser-side filter finds only what is already visible.
147	
148	**The phrase waits ~250 ms before it travels.** Without that every character is a separate
149	request, the answers race, and the one that came back last wins.
150	
151	**Changing the phrase or the order resets the number of entries shown.** Otherwise twelve
152	loaded entries become twelve results for a phrase that matches two — and the other way round, a
153	narrow piece reads as "that is all".
154	
155	**The question lives in the address**, not in a component's memory: `?q=`, `?sort=oldest`,
156	`?shown=8`. A result can be sent as a link and survives a reload. Every parameter is **absent at
157	its default value**, so an ordinary address is `/guestbook` rather than
158	`/guestbook?q=&sort=newest&shown=4`. A write **replaces** the history entry: a six-letter
159	phrase would otherwise leave six entries, and "back" would remove the letters one at a time.
160	
161	**The address is the source of truth, and the search field follows it.** A navigation — a link
162	followed in place, Back, Forward, the jump after a successful post — reseeds the field, and only
163	typing that happened after that navigation may write back. A phrase still waiting out its ~250 ms
164	when a navigation arrives is **cancelled**, never written. The other direction is a screen that
165	undoes the reader's own Back, and does it a quarter of a second later, where nothing connects the
166	two.
167	
168	**`?shown=` says how many entries are on screen**, not how big one request may be. The contract
169	caps a single read at 100 (`api.md` § Collection read parameters), so an address asking for more
170	is restored by **repeating the read** — each request inside that cap, none of them a refusal. The
171	number is still clamped, at ten reads' worth: an address typed by hand should show the guestbook,
172	and should not cost five hundred requests either.
173	
174	**The result sentence has two forms and they are two different questions.** Without a phrase:
175	`Showing 4 of 12` — how much of the guestbook is visible. With a phrase: `3 matches for "anna"` —
176	whether the search worked at all. The number matching is the count of **the whole population**,
177	not of the piece; deriving it from the length of the list is a defect nobody sees, because what
178	comes out of it is a plausible-looking number.
179	
180	**The sentence belongs to the answer on screen, not to the phrase in the field.** While a newer
181	question is travelling those are two different things, and a sentence assembled from one of each
182	says `2 matches for "Zzz"` over two entries that match nothing of the sort. The phrase quoted is
183	the one the visible entries came back for, and ` — updating…` says the answer is behind. After a
184	failed read the sentence says the read failed, rather than keeping numbers that no longer stand
185	for anything.
186	
187	### The entry card (`EntryCard`)
188	
189	| State | What is visible |
190	|---|---|
191	| `default` | the signature, the entry's age, "Edit" and "Delete", the message |
192	| `edited` | "· edited" joins the age |
193	| `editing` | two fields and "Save"/"Cancel" instead of the message; "Edit" says "Editing" |
194	| `saving` | "Saving…" and the fields locked on the card whose amendment is travelling; "Edit" locked on **every** card until it settles |
195	| `deleting` | "Deleting…", both actions locked |
196	
197	**Editing happens in the card.** The words somebody is correcting stay where they read them, and
198	the list does not run away from under them. At most **one** card is ever open: two at once is a
199	state this screen cannot settle.
200	
201	**An amendment in flight belongs to the entry it was sent for, and no editor may move while it
202	is.** "Edit" is closed on every card until the answer lands. Without that, opening a second card
203	mid-save moved the editor out from under the save: the answer closed whichever card happened to
204	be open by then, and the "Saving…" marker moved with it, so the entry actually being written
205	stopped being marked as written. The alternative — let the second card open and keep the marker
206	on the first — shows a "Saving…" on a card that is no longer an editor, which is a state with
207	nothing to read it on. The lock lasts exactly as long as the request.
208	
209	**The editor is remounted on the entry's key.** Without that a second editing session shows the
210	first entry's content — and nothing on screen says so.
211	
212	**"Save" is closed when a field is empty.** `BR-01` is about entries, not about how they came to
213	be: an amendment may not do what a new entry is forbidden.
214	
215	**The age is text, but the instant stays in the markup.** `<time dateTime="…">` carries the exact
216	moment; "2 hours ago" rounds. A card that rendered only words would lose when the entry was
217	really written.
218	
219	**"· edited" is derived** from comparing both instants (`BR-02`), not read from a column.
220	
221	### The list and its states
222	
223	| State | What is visible |
224	|---|---|
225	| `loading` | four skeletons in the shape of cards, never a blank screen |
226	| `empty (guestbook)` | "No entries yet. Be the first." in a dashed frame |
227	| `empty (search)` | "Nothing matches that search." — **a different sentence**, because a different fact |
228	| `error` | an `ErrorState` with `role="alert"` and a "Try again" action |
229	| `more` | a "Load N more" button, where N never promises more than is left |
230	
231	**"Be the first" in front of a guestbook full of entries reads like an application that has lost
232	them.** Hence two sentences, decided by whether the phrase is empty, not by whether the list is.
233	
234	**The list does not sort what it was given.** The order is the server's (`BR-04`); a list that
235	reorders the rows it received can disagree with paging and show an entry twice.
236	
237	**"Load more" appends the next piece, by `offset`.** Each press asks for the four entries after
238	the ones on screen and writes the new total into `?shown=`; the button goes away when `offset`
239	has reached the count that matched. An entry added or removed while several pieces are on screen
240	cannot duplicate or vanish, because every write invalidates the whole read and the pieces are
241	replayed from the first over the order as it now stands — the order is total (`BR-04`), so a piece
242	boundary is a place in it rather than a guess.
243	
244	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — this reverses a decision recorded in this
245	document, and it is recorded here rather than in `spec/ADR/` because
246	[`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR keeps that directory empty
247	until the first change goes through the process, and a rule with two homes is the failure it is
248	kept empty to avoid; the repair was made on the trunk and carries no `delta.md`):
249	
250	- **Keep asking for a bigger piece from the same start.** It was chosen because a growing window
251	  over a total order cannot duplicate or lose an entry while somebody writes, and that much was
252	  true. What it could not do was reach past the hundredth entry: the contract caps a single read
253	  at 100, so the window stopped growing there while `?shown=` went on counting, the read stopped
254	  changing with it, and "Load N more" stayed on screen for ever offering entries it could no
255	  longer fetch. A decision that holds only for guestbooks smaller than a hundred is not a decision
256	  about this guestbook. The property it was chosen for is kept by other means, named above.
257	- **Raise the cap on a single read.** It moves the wall rather than removing it, and it does so by
258	  making the API answer an unbounded page — a contract change paid for by every client, to buy a
259	  screen one that pages properly does not need.
260	
261	### The delete dialog (`DeleteEntryDialog`)
262	
263	| State | What is visible |
264	|---|---|
265	| `default` | the entry's signature and message, a sentence about irreversibility, two buttons |
266	| `loading` | "Deleting…", both buttons locked, the dialog **not closeable** |
267	
268	**The dialog quotes the entry it is about.** Cards differ only in their content, so a
269	confirmation that does not name what it will destroy cannot be answered correctly.
270	
271	**Focus lands on "Cancel", not on the destructive action.** An Enter pressed out of habit is to
272	delete nothing.
273	
274	**Focus lands *inside the dialog* in every state, and "Cancel" is the preference rather than the
275	promise.** In `loading` both buttons are locked, so there is nothing in the dialog that can hold
276	the keyboard except the dialog itself: focus goes to the `role="dialog"` container. The screen
277	asks whether the element it wanted actually took the focus rather than whether it exists — a
278	`disabled` button is a perfectly live element that silently refuses, and so are a hidden one, a
279	`display: none` one and one that has already left the page.
280	
281	**Tab cannot leave the dialog, from either direction, including when focus is already outside
282	it.** The cycle closes both ways; a Tab pressed with focus somewhere behind the modal brings it
283	back. The last condition is not hypothetical — it is what a browser leaves behind after the
284	element that opened the dialog goes away.
285	
286	**The rest of the page is inert while the dialog is open**, and is exactly as it was afterwards.
287	`aria-modal="true"` tells a screen reader the page behind is unavailable, and a reader given that
288	claim while focus is physically behind the dialog has two incompatible models of one page — worse
289	than never having claimed it.
290	
291	**Focus returns to whatever opened the dialog, and to the nearest thing still on screen when that
292	is gone.** A confirmed delete removes the card the "Delete" button sat in, so there is nothing to
293	hand focus back to; it goes to the closest ancestor still in the document — the list being read —
294	and never to `<body>`, from where the next Tab restarts at the top of the page.
295	
296	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — the mechanism was repaired from the trunk,
297	where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is available; `../conventions.md` § When a decision is an
298	ADR keeps `spec/ADR/` empty until the first change carried out through `/sdd`, so the decision is
299	recorded here, in the document whose rule it concerns):
300	
301	- **A native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`.** It would supply the backdrop, the inertness, the
302	  entering focus and Escape for nothing. Three things stand against it. It paints in the browser's
303	  **top layer**, over every z-index there is, and this application's toast host is an ordinary
304	  always-mounted `fixed` node — so `::backdrop` would cover the one region that has anything to
305	  say while the dialog is open, and a failed delete is announced exactly there. A `<dialog>`
306	  closes on Escape natively, so the `loading` row above — the dialog is **not closeable** while
307	  the request is in flight — costs an intercepted `cancel` event, which is the same amount of
308	  code as owning the key. And both `aria-live` regions are deliberately mounted at all times, so
309	  moving the dialog into the top layer changes what a reader observes about a region it is
310	  already watching. Revisit it together with the toast host, not on its own.
311	- **Leave the reason as it stood.** The component's own comment blamed "this app's
312	  `position: absolute` overlays", of which there is not one in the tree. A recorded reason that
313	  is false is worse than none: the next reader checks it, finds it wrong, and throws out the
314	  decision along with it.
315	
316	## Copy
317	
318	All of it here — it is product content rather than an implementation detail. The language is
319	settled by [`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Language.
320	
321	| Key | Text |
322	|---|---|
323	| screen title | `Leave a note` |
324	| introductory sentence | `No account, no sign-in. Write something, and it appears below straight away. Anyone can edit or remove an entry.` |
325	| entry count | `1 entry` / `7 entries` |
326	| signature placeholder | `Your name` |
327	| message placeholder | `Write your message…` |
328	| character counter | `0 / 1000` — code points of the trimmed, normalized message |
329	| post button | `Post entry` |
330	| button in flight | `Posting…` |
331	| search placeholder | `Search entries` |
332	| order | `Newest` · `Oldest` |
333	| result, no phrase | `Showing 4 of 12` |
334	| result, with phrase | `3 matches for “anna”` / `1 match for “anna”` |
335	| result, answer still travelling | the sentence above plus ` — updating…` |
336	| result, read failed | `The entries could not be loaded.` |
337	| card actions | `Edit` · `Delete` |
338	| card being edited | `Editing` |
339	| saving an amendment | `Save` · `Saving…` · `Cancel` |
340	| amendment marker | `· edited` |
341	| entry age | `just now` · `1 minute ago` · `2 hours ago` · `3 days ago` · `31 Aug 2026` |
342	| load more | `Load 4 more` |
343	| empty guestbook | `No entries yet. Be the first.` |
344	| empty search | `Nothing matches that search.` |
345	| dialog — title | `Delete this entry?` |
346	| dialog — quotation | `<signature> wrote:` |
347	| dialog — consequence | `This cannot be undone.` |
348	| dialog — confirmation | `Delete entry` · `Deleting…` · `Cancel` |
349	| toast after posting | `Entry posted.` |
350	| toast after amending | `Entry updated.` |
351	| toast after deleting | `Entry deleted.` |
352	| error — empty signature | `Add a name or a signature — an entry without one is not saved.` |
353	| error — empty message | `Write something — an empty entry is not saved.` |
354	| error — signature too long | `A signature can be at most 80 characters.` — the sentence says "characters" because that is the word a guest uses; the rule counts code points (`../../contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`) |
355	| error — message too long | `An entry can be at most 1000 characters.` |
356	
357	### Accessibility labels
358	
359	Text nobody sees and assistive technology reads — `aria-label`, the names of regions and states.
360	Here for the same reason as the rest, because a component test and the smoke look elements up by
361	them:
362	
363	| Text | Component |
364	|---|---|
365	| `Your message` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryComposer.tsx` |
366	| `Edit name` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryCard.tsx` |
367	| `Edit message` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryCard.tsx` |
368	| `Order` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryToolbar.tsx` |
369	| `Dismiss notification` | `frontend/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx` |
370	
371	The **server's** refusal sentences live beside the endpoint that produces them
372	([`../api.md`](../api.md) § Refusals): they are backend text rather than this screen's text. The
373	screen can display two of them: `guestbook_entry_not_found` (when somebody else deleted the entry
374	in the meantime) and `guestbook_entry_empty_patch`. Both are English, like everything else
375	(`../conventions.md` § Language); the router holds the sentences and this screen displays them.
376	
377	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-05, `cr: historical` — found by auditing this document against
378	`app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`, from the trunk, where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is
379	available):
380	
381	- **Leave the sentence as a harmless note.** A screen specification saying its refusal copy
382	  "is still written in Polish, and moves to English together with the router" is an
383	  instruction to the next author, in a document `design-ui` and `build-frontend` both read as
384	  the authority on copy. The move it promises happened before this document was last touched.
385	
386	## Data
387	
388	| What | From where |
389	|---|---|
390	| the phrase, the order, the piece size | the page address, through `useEntryQueryParams()` |
391	| a piece of the list + two numbers | `GET /api/guestbook-entries?q&sort&limit&offset` through `useGuestbookEntries()` |
392	| posting | `POST /api/guestbook-entries` through `useCreateGuestbookEntry()` |
393	| amending | `PATCH /api/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}` through `useUpdateGuestbookEntry()` |
394	| deleting | `DELETE /api/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}` through `useDeleteGuestbookEntry()` |
395	
396	**Components never call `client.GET` directly** — one hook per resource, the query keys in one
397	object (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Frontend). The list's key carries the phrase, the order
398	and the piece size, so two different questions are two cache entries rather than one that jumps
399	between two answers. Every mutation invalidates the resource's key, so a refresh corresponds to
400	something that really happened.
401	
402	## Interactions
403	
404	| Event | Effect |
405	|---|---|
406	| typing in the composer card | the button unlocks when both fields have content; the counter rises — over the **trimmed, normalized** message in code points, which is the string the validator beside it measures and the server will store. It read the raw value in UTF-16 units until 2026-09-17, so it could show `1000 / 1000` for a message the validator called shorter, and again for five hundred emoji |
407	| leaving a field | that field's error appears, if there is one |
408	| posting | a write; on success a toast, an empty card and a return to the clean address `/guestbook`; on failure a toast and **the text stays** |
409	| typing in the search field | after ~250 ms the phrase lands in the address and travels to the server, the number of entries shown returns to 4 |
410	| "Newest"/"Oldest" | the order lands in the address, a read from the other end of the guestbook, the number of entries shown returns to 4 |
411	| "Load N more" | the next piece is read from `offset`; `?shown=` in the address becomes the new total; the button disappears when nothing is left |
412	| arriving by a link with parameters | the screen starts exactly on what the link says, including the contents of the search field and how many entries are on screen |
413	| Back, Forward, or a link followed in place | the address wins: the search field is reseeded from it and a phrase still waiting out its pause is cancelled rather than written |
414	| "Edit" | the card opens an editor with **this** entry's content; the previously open one closes |
415	| "Edit" while an amendment is in flight | nothing — the action is locked on every card until that amendment settles |
416	| "Cancel" | the editor disappears, the entry is unchanged |
417	| "Save" | an amendment; on success a toast and the card returns to reading |
418	| "Delete" | opens the dialog |
419	| confirming in the dialog | deletion; an entry being edited, if it is the same one, stops being edited |
420	| Escape / clicking the backdrop | closes the dialog — **except** while a deletion is in flight |
421	
422	## Tokens
423	
424	The shared rules: [`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens.
425	
426	## Out of scope for this screen
427	
428	- **Anything to do with identity.** There is no sign-in, no "my entry", no avatar.
429	- **A mobile view.** The column narrows with the window, but it is not designed for a phone.
430

---
screen: guestbook
route: /guestbook
info_ref: S-01
requirements: [CR-2609-9b1e/R-1, CR-2609-9b1e/R-2, CR-2609-9b1e/R-3, CR-2609-9b1e/R-4, CR-2609-9b1e/R-5, CR-2609-9b1e/R-6, CR-2609-9b1e/R-7]
mockup: null
---

# Guestbook

The only screen of this application. A guest opens it, reads what others wrote, and adds an
entry of their own; they can also find an entry, view the guestbook a piece at a time, and amend
or delete any entry — including somebody else's, because there is no identity here
([`../../contexts/guestbook.md`](../../contexts/guestbook.md) § Deliberate non-goals).

The screen was built from a Claude Design mock-up
([`spec/rationale/mockup-guestbook/Guestbook.dc.html`](../../rationale/mockup-guestbook/Guestbook.dc.html)):
one centred column on a cream background, a serif title, a dark green accent.

`mockup: null`, and that is **a record of a fact rather than an absence**: the mock-up arrived in
an archive outside the SDD process, and [`README.md`](README.md) § HTML is the evidence foresees
one place for it — `spec/changes/<CR>/design/ui/index.html` — which this change does not have,
because it opened no change record. A field pointing at a file that is not in the repository
would be worse than an empty one. The first change to this screen carried out through `/sdd` will
put the mock-up where it belongs and fill this field in.

The mock-up differs from what was built in two places, and **both are deliberate**:

1. **A signature is required.** The mock-up substituted "Anonymous" for an empty signature;
   `BR-01` does not allow for that, and changing a business rule is not changing an appearance.
2. **Deleting asks.** The mock-up deletes outright on a click; `BR-03` is irreversible, and a
   layout drawing is not a decision to remove the only warning.

The frame, the palette, the typeface and the primitives: [`system-states.md`](system-states.md).

## Regions

Top to bottom, inside the page frame:

1. **Header and title** — the lockup, the number of entries in the whole guestbook, the title
   "Leave a note" and a sentence saying there is no sign-in here.
2. **The composer card** (`EntryComposer`) — signature, message, length counter, button.
3. **The toolbar** (`EntryToolbar`) — a search field, two order pills, and beneath them one
   sentence about the result.
4. **The list of cards** (`EntryCard`) — one entry is one card, with two actions and **in-place
   editing**.
5. **The load-more button** — only when something is left.
6. **The confirmation dialog** (`DeleteEntryDialog`) — above the screen, only when deleting.

## Components and their states

### The composer card (`EntryComposer`)

| State | What is visible |
|---|---|
| `default` | two empty fields with no border, the counter `0 / 1000`, the button **`disabled`** |
| `focus` | a focus ring in the accent colour; no change of layout |
| `error` | a sentence under the field, `role="alert"`, `aria-invalid` on the field |
| `disabled` | both fields and the button locked while a write is in flight |
| `loading` | the button says "Posting…"; the card stays on screen, it does not disappear |

**The fields have no visible label**, as in the mock-up — two placeholders in a card that is
obviously a form. They do carry an `aria-label`: a placeholder on its own is a label that
disappears at exactly the moment somebody starts typing.

**The placeholder is therefore text under WCAG 1.4.3, not decoration**, and is held to the same
4.5:1 floor as everything else ([`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens). It is the only
thing on screen saying what goes in the field.

**The focus ring is the screen's, and no component may cancel it.** It is declared once, in
`frontend/src/index.css`, on `:focus-visible` inside `@layer base` — and a Tailwind utility on
the element (`outline-none`) beats it whatever its specificity, because `@layer utilities` is a
**later layer** and layer order settles the cascade before specificity is consulted. A field that
wants a different ring says so with a `focus-visible:outline-*` utility, which competes inside
the same layer; it never removes the ring and leaves nothing.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — found by measuring the *built* stylesheet,
from the trunk, where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is available):

- **Strengthen the base rule instead — `!important`, a heavier selector.** Neither reaches it.
  The rule matched and lost on one property in a later layer, so no amount of specificity
  changes the outcome; the only cure at that level is to move the ring into `@layer utilities`,
  which would put the screen's one accessibility guarantee in the layer components write to.
- **Assert the ring in `vitest`.** The component suite runs in jsdom, which loads no application
  CSS, implements no `@layer`, and does not support `:focus-visible` — a test for the ring's
  presence in the *source* would have passed on a screen with no visible ring at all, which is
  exactly the state the repository was in. The assertion belongs in a browser: `e2e/ui/`.

**An error appears only after the field is left**, never on every character. Telling somebody
their signature is too short at the first letter is noise — and noise is what teaches people to
ignore red text that means something real.

**No field stops accepting input at its bound; the message under it is the bound.** Both fields
carried `maxLength` until 2026-09-17 and it was removed on purpose. The HTML attribute counts
UTF-16 code units, which nothing else in this system counts, so the signature field stopped
accepting characters after 40 emoji rather than 80 — and it stopped *silently*, which is the
worst of the three symptoms the bound had: the guest loses what they typed with no sentence
anywhere saying why. A validator message a person can read is the whole remedy, and it now
counts the same code points the server counts.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — taken outside `/forge:sdd` on GitHub issue
#28, so there is no `delta.md` in which to declare it):

- **Keep `maxLength` as a generous safety valve (×4).** It would still truncate silently, only
  later and at a number matching no rule anywhere. A cap nobody can predict is worse than no cap
  for the person meeting it.
- **Clamp on paste to the code-point bound.** A visible, correct hard stop — but it is a fourth
  place that measures text, it needs a screen state of its own to explain itself, and the
  message under the field already says the same thing without any of that.
- **Leave it and fix only the validator.** The two would then disagree about the same field: the
  message would say 80 while the field accepted 40. That is the defect, not a smaller version
  of it.

**The button is `disabled` until both fields have content.** The rule lives in
`frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/lib/guestbookEntry.ts`; the screen only applies it.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — the two files this document cites moved
when the tree was recut by bounded context. The decision itself is
[`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Frontend — where a file goes and
[`../architecture.md`](../architecture.md) § What a new feature adds; this edit is only its
consequence, and it is recorded because the edit was made from the trunk, where no `delta.md`
exists to call it editorial):

- **Leave the citations pointing at the old paths.** They resolve to nothing, and
  `backtick-paths` says so on every pull request. A screen specification pointing at a file
  that is not there is precisely the drift between screen and specification this document
  exists to prevent — and the rule it points at did not move, only the file did.

**The card clears after a successful post and does not clear after a failed one.** The first, so
that the next guest does not send somebody else's entry a second time. The second, because a
form that empties its fields after an error is a form nobody retries.

**After a successful post the screen returns to the unfiltered guestbook, newest first.** An
entry sent while searching would land outside the result, and an entry you cannot see looks like
an entry that was not saved.

### The toolbar (`EntryToolbar`)

| State | What is visible |
|---|---|
| `default` | an empty search field, "Newest" selected |
| `searching` | the typed phrase, the result sentence says how many match |
| `stale` | the previous answer stays on screen, its sentence carries ` — updating…`, and the live region is `aria-busy` |

**Search asks the server, it does not filter an array on screen.** An entry that did not fit in
the first piece must be findable — a browser-side filter finds only what is already visible.

**The phrase waits ~250 ms before it travels.** Without that every character is a separate
request, the answers race, and the one that came back last wins.

**Changing the phrase or the order resets the number of entries shown.** Otherwise twelve
loaded entries become twelve results for a phrase that matches two — and the other way round, a
narrow piece reads as "that is all".

**The question lives in the address**, not in a component's memory: `?q=`, `?sort=oldest`,
`?shown=8`. A result can be sent as a link and survives a reload. Every parameter is **absent at
its default value**, so an ordinary address is `/guestbook` rather than
`/guestbook?q=&sort=newest&shown=4`. A write **replaces** the history entry: a six-letter
phrase would otherwise leave six entries, and "back" would remove the letters one at a time.

**The address is the source of truth, and the search field follows it.** A navigation — a link
followed in place, Back, Forward, the jump after a successful post — reseeds the field, and only
typing that happened after that navigation may write back. A phrase still waiting out its ~250 ms
when a navigation arrives is **cancelled**, never written. The other direction is a screen that
undoes the reader's own Back, and does it a quarter of a second later, where nothing connects the
two.

**`?shown=` says how many entries are on screen**, not how big one request may be. The contract
caps a single read at 100 (`api.md` § Collection read parameters), so an address asking for more
is restored by **repeating the read** — each request inside that cap, none of them a refusal. The
number is still clamped, at ten reads' worth: an address typed by hand should show the guestbook,
and should not cost five hundred requests either.

**The result sentence has two forms and they are two different questions.** Without a phrase:
`Showing 4 of 12` — how much of the guestbook is visible. With a phrase: `3 matches for "anna"` —
whether the search worked at all. The number matching is the count of **the whole population**,
not of the piece; deriving it from the length of the list is a defect nobody sees, because what
comes out of it is a plausible-looking number.

**The sentence belongs to the answer on screen, not to the phrase in the field.** While a newer
question is travelling those are two different things, and a sentence assembled from one of each
says `2 matches for "Zzz"` over two entries that match nothing of the sort. The phrase quoted is
the one the visible entries came back for, and ` — updating…` says the answer is behind. After a
failed read the sentence says the read failed, rather than keeping numbers that no longer stand
for anything.

### The entry card (`EntryCard`)

| State | What is visible |
|---|---|
| `default` | the signature, the entry's age, "Edit" and "Delete", the message |
| `edited` | "· edited" joins the age |
| `editing` | two fields and "Save"/"Cancel" instead of the message; "Edit" says "Editing" |
| `saving` | "Saving…" and the fields locked on the card whose amendment is travelling; "Edit" locked on **every** card until it settles |
| `deleting` | "Deleting…", both actions locked |

**Editing happens in the card.** The words somebody is correcting stay where they read them, and
the list does not run away from under them. At most **one** card is ever open: two at once is a
state this screen cannot settle.

**An amendment in flight belongs to the entry it was sent for, and no editor may move while it
is.** "Edit" is closed on every card until the answer lands. Without that, opening a second card
mid-save moved the editor out from under the save: the answer closed whichever card happened to
be open by then, and the "Saving…" marker moved with it, so the entry actually being written
stopped being marked as written. The alternative — let the second card open and keep the marker
on the first — shows a "Saving…" on a card that is no longer an editor, which is a state with
nothing to read it on. The lock lasts exactly as long as the request.

**The editor is remounted on the entry's key.** Without that a second editing session shows the
first entry's content — and nothing on screen says so.

**"Save" is closed when a field is empty.** `BR-01` is about entries, not about how they came to
be: an amendment may not do what a new entry is forbidden.

**The age is text, but the instant stays in the markup.** `<time dateTime="…">` carries the exact
moment; "2 hours ago" rounds. A card that rendered only words would lose when the entry was
really written.

**"· edited" is derived** from comparing both instants (`BR-02`), not read from a column.

### The list and its states

| State | What is visible |
|---|---|
| `loading` | four skeletons in the shape of cards, never a blank screen |
| `empty (guestbook)` | "No entries yet. Be the first." in a dashed frame |
| `empty (search)` | "Nothing matches that search." — **a different sentence**, because a different fact |
| `error` | an `ErrorState` with `role="alert"` and a "Try again" action |
| `more` | a "Load N more" button, where N never promises more than is left |

**"Be the first" in front of a guestbook full of entries reads like an application that has lost
them.** Hence two sentences, decided by whether the phrase is empty, not by whether the list is.

**The list does not sort what it was given.** The order is the server's (`BR-04`); a list that
reorders the rows it received can disagree with paging and show an entry twice.

**"Load more" appends the next piece, by `offset`.** Each press asks for the four entries after
the ones on screen and writes the new total into `?shown=`; the button goes away when `offset`
has reached the count that matched. An entry added or removed while several pieces are on screen
cannot duplicate or vanish, because every write invalidates the whole read and the pieces are
replayed from the first over the order as it now stands — the order is total (`BR-04`), so a piece
boundary is a place in it rather than a guess.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — this reverses a decision recorded in this
document, and it is recorded here rather than in `spec/ADR/` because
[`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § When a decision is an ADR keeps that directory empty
until the first change goes through the process, and a rule with two homes is the failure it is
kept empty to avoid; the repair was made on the trunk and carries no `delta.md`):

- **Keep asking for a bigger piece from the same start.** It was chosen because a growing window
  over a total order cannot duplicate or lose an entry while somebody writes, and that much was
  true. What it could not do was reach past the hundredth entry: the contract caps a single read
  at 100, so the window stopped growing there while `?shown=` went on counting, the read stopped
  changing with it, and "Load N more" stayed on screen for ever offering entries it could no
  longer fetch. A decision that holds only for guestbooks smaller than a hundred is not a decision
  about this guestbook. The property it was chosen for is kept by other means, named above.
- **Raise the cap on a single read.** It moves the wall rather than removing it, and it does so by
  making the API answer an unbounded page — a contract change paid for by every client, to buy a
  screen one that pages properly does not need.

### The delete dialog (`DeleteEntryDialog`)

| State | What is visible |
|---|---|
| `default` | the entry's signature and message, a sentence about irreversibility, two buttons |
| `loading` | "Deleting…", both buttons locked, the dialog **not closeable** |

**The dialog quotes the entry it is about.** Cards differ only in their content, so a
confirmation that does not name what it will destroy cannot be answered correctly.

**Focus lands on "Cancel", not on the destructive action.** An Enter pressed out of habit is to
delete nothing.

**Focus lands *inside the dialog* in every state, and "Cancel" is the preference rather than the
promise.** In `loading` both buttons are locked, so there is nothing in the dialog that can hold
the keyboard except the dialog itself: focus goes to the `role="dialog"` container. The screen
asks whether the element it wanted actually took the focus rather than whether it exists — a
`disabled` button is a perfectly live element that silently refuses, and so are a hidden one, a
`display: none` one and one that has already left the page.

**Tab cannot leave the dialog, from either direction, including when focus is already outside
it.** The cycle closes both ways; a Tab pressed with focus somewhere behind the modal brings it
back. The last condition is not hypothetical — it is what a browser leaves behind after the
element that opened the dialog goes away.

**The rest of the page is inert while the dialog is open**, and is exactly as it was afterwards.
`aria-modal="true"` tells a screen reader the page behind is unavailable, and a reader given that
claim while focus is physically behind the dialog has two incompatible models of one page — worse
than never having claimed it.

**Focus returns to whatever opened the dialog, and to the nearest thing still on screen when that
is gone.** A confirmed delete removes the card the "Delete" button sat in, so there is nothing to
hand focus back to; it goes to the closest ancestor still in the document — the list being read —
and never to `<body>`, from where the next Tab restarts at the top of the page.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-16, `cr: historical` — the mechanism was repaired from the trunk,
where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is available; `../conventions.md` § When a decision is an
ADR keeps `spec/ADR/` empty until the first change carried out through `/sdd`, so the decision is
recorded here, in the document whose rule it concerns):

- **A native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`.** It would supply the backdrop, the inertness, the
  entering focus and Escape for nothing. Three things stand against it. It paints in the browser's
  **top layer**, over every z-index there is, and this application's toast host is an ordinary
  always-mounted `fixed` node — so `::backdrop` would cover the one region that has anything to
  say while the dialog is open, and a failed delete is announced exactly there. A `<dialog>`
  closes on Escape natively, so the `loading` row above — the dialog is **not closeable** while
  the request is in flight — costs an intercepted `cancel` event, which is the same amount of
  code as owning the key. And both `aria-live` regions are deliberately mounted at all times, so
  moving the dialog into the top layer changes what a reader observes about a region it is
  already watching. Revisit it together with the toast host, not on its own.
- **Leave the reason as it stood.** The component's own comment blamed "this app's
  `position: absolute` overlays", of which there is not one in the tree. A recorded reason that
  is false is worse than none: the next reader checks it, finds it wrong, and throws out the
  decision along with it.

## Copy

All of it here — it is product content rather than an implementation detail. The language is
settled by [`../conventions.md`](../conventions.md) § Language.

| Key | Text |
|---|---|
| screen title | `Leave a note` |
| introductory sentence | `No account, no sign-in. Write something, and it appears below straight away. Anyone can edit or remove an entry.` |
| entry count | `1 entry` / `7 entries` |
| signature placeholder | `Your name` |
| message placeholder | `Write your message…` |
| character counter | `0 / 1000` — code points of the trimmed, normalized message |
| post button | `Post entry` |
| button in flight | `Posting…` |
| search placeholder | `Search entries` |
| order | `Newest` · `Oldest` |
| result, no phrase | `Showing 4 of 12` |
| result, with phrase | `3 matches for “anna”` / `1 match for “anna”` |
| result, answer still travelling | the sentence above plus ` — updating…` |
| result, read failed | `The entries could not be loaded.` |
| card actions | `Edit` · `Delete` |
| card being edited | `Editing` |
| saving an amendment | `Save` · `Saving…` · `Cancel` |
| amendment marker | `· edited` |
| entry age | `just now` · `1 minute ago` · `2 hours ago` · `3 days ago` · `31 Aug 2026` |
| load more | `Load 4 more` |
| empty guestbook | `No entries yet. Be the first.` |
| empty search | `Nothing matches that search.` |
| dialog — title | `Delete this entry?` |
| dialog — quotation | `<signature> wrote:` |
| dialog — consequence | `This cannot be undone.` |
| dialog — confirmation | `Delete entry` · `Deleting…` · `Cancel` |
| toast after posting | `Entry posted.` |
| toast after amending | `Entry updated.` |
| toast after deleting | `Entry deleted.` |
| error — empty signature | `Add a name or a signature — an entry without one is not saved.` |
| error — empty message | `Write something — an empty entry is not saved.` |
| error — signature too long | `A signature can be at most 80 characters.` — the sentence says "characters" because that is the word a guest uses; the rule counts code points (`../../contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01`) |
| error — message too long | `An entry can be at most 1000 characters.` |

### Accessibility labels

Text nobody sees and assistive technology reads — `aria-label`, the names of regions and states.
Here for the same reason as the rest, because a component test and the smoke look elements up by
them:

| Text | Component |
|---|---|
| `Your message` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryComposer.tsx` |
| `Edit name` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryCard.tsx` |
| `Edit message` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryCard.tsx` |
| `Order` | `frontend/src/contexts/guestbook/components/EntryToolbar.tsx` |
| `Dismiss notification` | `frontend/src/components/ui/Toast.tsx` |

The **server's** refusal sentences live beside the endpoint that produces them
([`../api.md`](../api.md) § Refusals): they are backend text rather than this screen's text. The
screen can display two of them: `guestbook_entry_not_found` (when somebody else deleted the entry
in the meantime) and `guestbook_entry_empty_patch`. Both are English, like everything else
(`../conventions.md` § Language); the router holds the sentences and this screen displays them.

Rejected (decision of 2026-09-05, `cr: historical` — found by auditing this document against
`app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`, from the trunk, where neither an ADR nor a `delta.md` is
available):

- **Leave the sentence as a harmless note.** A screen specification saying its refusal copy
  "is still written in Polish, and moves to English together with the router" is an
  instruction to the next author, in a document `design-ui` and `build-frontend` both read as
  the authority on copy. The move it promises happened before this document was last touched.

## Data

| What | From where |
|---|---|
| the phrase, the order, the piece size | the page address, through `useEntryQueryParams()` |
| a piece of the list + two numbers | `GET /api/guestbook-entries?q&sort&limit&offset` through `useGuestbookEntries()` |
| posting | `POST /api/guestbook-entries` through `useCreateGuestbookEntry()` |
| amending | `PATCH /api/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}` through `useUpdateGuestbookEntry()` |
| deleting | `DELETE /api/guestbook-entries/{entry_id}` through `useDeleteGuestbookEntry()` |

**Components never call `client.GET` directly** — one hook per resource, the query keys in one
object (`spec/design/conventions.md` § Frontend). The list's key carries the phrase, the order
and the piece size, so two different questions are two cache entries rather than one that jumps
between two answers. Every mutation invalidates the resource's key, so a refresh corresponds to
something that really happened.

## Interactions

| Event | Effect |
|---|---|
| typing in the composer card | the button unlocks when both fields have content; the counter rises — over the **trimmed, normalized** message in code points, which is the string the validator beside it measures and the server will store. It read the raw value in UTF-16 units until 2026-09-17, so it could show `1000 / 1000` for a message the validator called shorter, and again for five hundred emoji |
| leaving a field | that field's error appears, if there is one |
| posting | a write; on success a toast, an empty card and a return to the clean address `/guestbook`; on failure a toast and **the text stays** |
| typing in the search field | after ~250 ms the phrase lands in the address and travels to the server, the number of entries shown returns to 4 |
| "Newest"/"Oldest" | the order lands in the address, a read from the other end of the guestbook, the number of entries shown returns to 4 |
| "Load N more" | the next piece is read from `offset`; `?shown=` in the address becomes the new total; the button disappears when nothing is left |
| arriving by a link with parameters | the screen starts exactly on what the link says, including the contents of the search field and how many entries are on screen |
| Back, Forward, or a link followed in place | the address wins: the search field is reseeded from it and a phrase still waiting out its pause is cancelled rather than written |
| "Edit" | the card opens an editor with **this** entry's content; the previously open one closes |
| "Edit" while an amendment is in flight | nothing — the action is locked on every card until that amendment settles |
| "Cancel" | the editor disappears, the entry is unchanged |
| "Save" | an amendment; on success a toast and the card returns to reading |
| "Delete" | opens the dialog |
| confirming in the dialog | deletion; an entry being edited, if it is the same one, stops being edited |
| Escape / clicking the backdrop | closes the dialog — **except** while a deletion is in flight |

## Tokens

The shared rules: [`system-states.md`](system-states.md) § Tokens.

## Out of scope for this screen

- **Anything to do with identity.** There is no sign-in, no "my entry", no avatar.
- **A mobile view.** The column narrows with the window, but it is not designed for a phone.

# Drop box — input material for this change

This directory is your drop box. Put everything you have about this change here — the
process reads every file in this directory before it starts writing the specification.
Any format: `.md` or `.txt` notes, screenshots, an Excel file with an example.

## What to drop in

1. **Requirement notes** — in your own words. The more concrete they are, the fewer
   questions you get later.
2. **New test data** — files showing the case this change is about, shaped like the ones
   in the project's own reference corpus, when it keeps one.
   The data has to be synthetic: no real names, addresses or account numbers.
3. **A Claude Design mockup** — an HTML file with the designed view. That one file does
   NOT go here: save it as `design/ui/index.html` (the directory next to `input/`).

## The minimum the process wants to know

- **What data the change processes** — new fields? changes to existing fields?
- **The process step by step** — what happens, in what order, who sees what.
- **A list of test scenarios** — in words, one sentence each: "when X, then Y".
- **Functional and non-functional requirements** — what has to work and how fast/safely.
- **What this change does NOT do** — the exclusions outside the scope. This is the most
  important point: silent scope is how an author and a reviewer agree on two different
  things.

## When you are done

Write **go on** or **build the specification** in the chat. If the drop box stays empty,
the process will ask you these questions one by one in conversation (the brainstorm stage)
— that works too, just more slowly.

content.content:
1	# Conventions
2	
3	Where a file goes, what it is called and what it may import. These are rules, not taste: each
4	is here because its absence produced a defect, and changing any of them needs an ADR exactly
5	as any other rule under `spec/design/` does.
6	
7	What the system *is* — its contexts, containers and flows — is described by
8	[`architecture.md`](architecture.md). How it is run, tested and developed is stated by
9	[`CLAUDE.md`](../../CLAUDE.md).
10	
11	## Layers
12	
13	Layering is strict and one-directional:
14	
15	```
16	app/contexts/<name>/ or app/platform/
17	  routers/   HTTP only: binding path/query/body, status codes, dependency injection
18	     ↓
19	  services/  business rules, transactions, the whole data-loading pipeline
20	     ↓
21	  models/    declarative SQLAlchemy mappings
22	  schemas/   Pydantic request and response contracts (never reused as ORM models)
23	```
24	
25	**The layer is a directory inside a slice, never above one** (§ Backend — where a file goes).
26	Layering itself is unchanged by that; only the depth at which the directories are found.
27	
28	**`services/`, `models/` and `schemas/` may not import `fastapi` or `starlette`.** Every module
29	in those packages says so in its docstring. This is what keeps business rules testable without
30	HTTP and reusable from an Alembic migration and a CLI script. Checked by
31	`tests/fitness/test_layering.py`.
32	
33	**Dependencies point one way**: `routers` → `services` → `models`/`schemas`. A service
34	importing a router, or a model importing a service, is a defect.
35	
36	A service **never names a status code**. It raises a domain exception; the router translates it,
37	explicitly, in a `match` block. `app/core/errors.py` registers three *framework* handlers and
38	knows nothing about the domain. The sentence an operator reads belongs beside the endpoint that
39	produced it, not in a shared table one edit away from telling somebody the wrong column to
40	correct. The worked example is `_not_found` in `app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`.
41	
42	## Backend — where a file goes
43	
44	**The outermost cut is the bounded context; the layer is a directory inside it.** A new domain
45	concept adds **one file per layer, named after the concept**, under the context that owns it —
46	`app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py`,
47	`app/contexts/guestbook/schemas/guestbook_entries.py`,
48	`app/contexts/guestbook/services/guestbook_entries.py`,
49	`app/contexts/guestbook/routers/guestbook_entries.py`. Never `utils.py`, `helpers.py` or
50	`common.py`: a name that describes nothing attracts everything.
51	
52	The reason the context is outermost is **ownership**, not taste. `.github/CODEOWNERS` matches
53	paths, so a tree cut by layer can hand somebody every context's `services/` — a quarter of each —
54	and can never hand them one context. A path that holds one context and nothing else is what
55	makes a context something a person or a team can be given.
56	
57	```
58	app/
59	  main.py            the composition root: middleware, the router, the assets, the SPA shell
60	  api.py             the one place the `/api` prefix is applied; one line per context
61	  contexts/<name>/   a bounded context and everything of it: models schemas services routers
62	  platform/          the supporting technical slice — HTTP with no domain rules in it
63	  core/  db/         infrastructure used by Platform and by every context alike
64	```
65	
66	- **`app/contexts/<name>/__init__.py`** — the context's **public API**. Another context may
67	  import `app.contexts.<name>` and nothing below it; `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py`
68	  refuses the rest. Importing it imports the context's models, which is what registers its
69	  tables on the shared `Base`.
70	- **`app/api.py`** — the aggregate, and **the `/api` prefix is applied there and nowhere else**,
71	  so a router registered anywhere else lands outside `/api` and is swallowed by the SPA
72	  catch-all. It is the **composition root**: the one module allowed to reach a context's router
73	  module, because a neighbouring context has business with a `GuestbookEntry` and none whatever
74	  with the function that binds it to a URL. One line per context, listed rather than
75	  discovered — so the registration can be checked in both directions.
76	- **`app/contexts/<name>/routers/`** — HTTP binding only, one module per resource, each
77	  exposing `router`. `guestbook` is the **only** domain context of this template and at the
78	  same time its worked example through every layer: copy it, and when your own context replaces
79	  it, delete it.
80	- **`app/contexts/<name>/services/`** — business rules. Owns the session and the transaction
81	  boundary.
82	- **`app/contexts/<name>/models/` + `alembic/versions/`** — one class per file, `Base` from
83	  `app/db/base.py`. Every schema change is a revision; `create_all()` is never called. Domain
84	  constants the whole application must agree on live beside the model they describe
85	  (`AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` in `app/contexts/guestbook/models/guestbook_entry.py`). See
86	  [`data-model.md`](data-model.md).
87	- **`app/contexts/<name>/schemas/`** — Pydantic request and response models, the file name
88	  plural per resource, the classes suffixed (`GuestbookEntryRead`, `GuestbookEntryCreate`).
89	  Read and write shapes are separate classes even when they are identical today. See
90	  [`api.md`](api.md).
91	- **`app/platform/`** — the technical slice: liveness, the health shape, the refusal envelope
92	  and the text rule. **Two files here are not named after a resource, and that is a rule rather
93	  than an exception to one.** `app/platform/schemas/refusals.py` carries the refusal envelope
94	  with a code, which is a fact about EVERY refusal this API makes rather than about guestbook
95	  entries; the sentences themselves stay beside the endpoint that produces them, and only the
96	  envelope is shared. `app/platform/schemas/text.py` carries how a text field is normalized,
97	  trimmed and measured, which is a fact about EVERY text field this API accepts; the *bounds*
98	  stay where their domain is (`AUTHOR_MAX_LENGTH` beside the model) and only the unit they
99	  count in is shared. The test of whether a third file belongs here is the same both times: not
100	  "is it generic" but "is it a fact about every one of these, rather than about one context's". `app/core/` and `app/db/` are **not** under this name, because they are used by
101	  Platform and by every context alike and filing them under one slice would say something
102	  untrue about who they belong to.
103	- **`tests/<group>/test_<subject>.py`** — one of four groups, with no mirroring of the package
104	  tree inside any of them. `unit/` does not touch the database, `integration/` needs it,
105	  `fitness/` reads this repository's source as text, `tooling/` covers `scripts/` and the
106	  end-to-end harness. **The directory is a declaration**: each of the three database-free groups
107	  carries a `conftest.py` that applies `no_db` to everything below it, so the marker cannot be
108	  forgotten, and `tests/fitness/test_test_layout.py` proves the converse. Shared helpers stay
109	  flat as `tests/_<subject>.py`. Reference data in `golden-set/`, located by
110	  `tests/_golden_set.py`, and the repository root by `tests/_repo.py` — never by counting
111	  directories, which broke eleven modules at once the first time the suite was grouped.
112	  **`golden-set/` is itself two declarations**: `fixtures/` is what a suite reads and asserts
113	  about, `seed/` is what a new environment opens with — the same rule as the test groups, one
114	  directory up. See [`testing.md`](testing.md).
115	- **One exception, and only one**: the tests of the SDD framework itself live beside the code
116	  they prove, as the engine's own tests. Most of them read their subject's
117	  *source* — which module defines a constant, which imports `fcntl`, which counts directories to
118	  find the repository root — and a check that reads source belongs beside it. The same `pytest`
119	  run collects them (`testpaths` names both roots), so this is an exception of layout rather
120	  than a second suite. The application's tests stay flat under `tests/`; this exception does not
121	  generalise.
122	
123	**Placeholder columns stay unwritten**: a column whose owning feature has not landed is nullable
124	and no service writes it; the docstring names the blocking feature.
125	
126	## Frontend — where a file goes
127	
128	**Cut by context first, exactly as the backend is**, because a screen is owned by the context
129	whose rules it shows, and because the same argument about `.github/CODEOWNERS` applies on this
130	side of the wire. What is left at the top level is what genuinely belongs to no context.
131	
132	```
133	frontend/src/
134	  contexts/<name>/   pages components hooks lib — one context's screen and everything of it
135	  components/ui/     design-system primitives, no business logic
136	  components/shell/  the frame every screen renders itself inside
137	  hooks/  lib/       rules and helpers that are about no context in particular
138	  api/               the generated contract and the client over it
139	  router.tsx         the composition root: the one module that binds a path to a screen
140	  routes.ts          the route constants, shared by the shell, the 404 page and the screen
141	```
142	
143	- **`frontend/src/contexts/<name>/`** — one context's screen and everything only it uses:
144	  `pages/<Name>Page.tsx`, its `components/`, its `hooks/`, its `lib/`. A module here may not
145	  import another context's folder; `tests/fitness/test_context_boundaries.py` refuses it, and
146	  `router.tsx` is the one named exception because binding a path to a screen is what a
147	  composition root does.
148	- **`frontend/src/pages/`** — screens belonging to no context: today `StatusPages.tsx`, which
149	  is what a wrong address gets. A screen that shows a context's rules belongs in that context.
150	  **Route paths are English** (`/guestbook`), like everything else in this repository
151	  (§ Language), and they live in `frontend/src/routes.ts` — a route is the application's
152	  composition rather than a context's internals, which is why a shared layout component no
153	  longer owns one.
154	- **`frontend/src/components/ui/`** — design-system primitives, no business logic, no data
155	  fetching. Export the component **and** its props interface. **Encode intent in variants, not
156	  in callers**: the `red` variant of `Banner` means "this is a loss, not a warning", and that is
157	  why an irreversible message cannot accidentally be made to look like an ordinary one. **A
158	  primitive with no caller is removed**, not kept in reserve: a component nobody renders is a
159	  branch nobody reviews against a screen.
160	- **`frontend/src/hooks/`** — two kinds, both tied to React. One TanStack Query hook per resource
161	  (`use<Resource>.ts`, exporting a `<resource>Keys` object; **components never call `client.GET`
162	  directly**) and hooks for state in the URL — filters, sorting and paging live in the address,
163	  so a screen can be shared and survives a reload (`useEntryQueryParams.ts`). A parameter at its
164	  default value is **absent** from the address, and a write replaces the history entry rather
165	  than adding one. The *rules* those hooks apply live in `lib/`.
166	- **`frontend/src/lib/`** — pure rules and formatting that belong to no context, one concern
167	  per file, named after it (`datetime.ts`, `relativeTime.ts`, `number.ts`, `cn.ts`). A rule
168	  about one context's data lives in that context's `lib/`
169	  (`contexts/guestbook/lib/guestbookEntry.ts`, `contexts/guestbook/lib/entryListCopy.ts`,
170	  `contexts/guestbook/lib/entryText.ts`), and moves up here the day a second context needs it —
171	  never before, because a shared module with one caller is a boundary drawn in the wrong place.
172	  `entryText.ts` is the case worth naming: its Python counterpart sits in `app/platform/`
173	  because the server has more than one caller for it, and this one stays in the context because
174	  the browser has exactly one. The asymmetry is each tree following its own rule rather than an
175	  oversight in either.
176	
177	  Rejected (decision of 2026-09-17, `cr: historical` — where the two halves of the text rule go,
178	  decided on GitHub issue #28, outside `/forge:sdd`):
179	
180	  - **Put both in the context, and add no file to `app/platform/`.** It keeps the trees
181	    symmetrical and says something untrue: how this API trims and measures text is a fact about
182	    every text field it accepts, and the schemas and the service are already two callers. The
183	    next context would copy the rule rather than import it, which is how a shared fact becomes
184	    two facts.
185	  - **Put both above the contexts, in `app/platform/` and `frontend/src/lib/`.** Symmetrical the
186	    other way, and it breaks this section's own rule: a shared module with one caller is a
187	    boundary drawn in the wrong place, and the browser has exactly one caller today.
188	  - **Fold the rule into `guestbookEntry.ts` rather than giving it a file.** The search phrase is
189	    not an entry, and it is measured by the same rule — so the module would be named after one of
190	    its two subjects. Never `format.ts` or `utils.ts`. Nothing
191	  here imports from `components/` or from `contexts/` — both are dependency arrows pointing
192	  backwards.
193	- **`frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts`** — generated, never edited. Domain types are aliased from it
194	  (`type GuestbookEntry = components['schemas']['GuestbookEntryRead']`). Regenerate rather than
195	  widen.
196	- **`frontend/src/styles/theme.css`** — the application's colour tokens and the only place where
197	  colour and typeface are written down. Everything that is neither — sizes, spacing, radii,
198	  shadows — comes from the Tailwind scale. A token name may not collide with a class name from
199	  that scale (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One palette). **Never a raw hex value or a
200	  bracketed value in a component** — a raw colour is a token nobody has named yet, and it is
201	  invisible to every later change of the palette.
202	
203	**Frontend tests** are `vitest`, `*.test.ts(x)` placed beside the module they test. The weight is
204	carried by the pure rules in `lib/` and the generated-contract adapters in `api/`; a component
205	test that asserts only that it rendered is noise.
206	
207	Screens are specified before they are built, one document per screen under [`ui/`](ui/) — that
208	rule, and the reason Markdown beats a mock-up, are given by [`ui/README.md`](ui/README.md).
209	
210	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-07, `cr: historical` — the placement rule changed from
211	layer-first to context-first, and this document is where placement rules live; the recut was

228	## Boundaries — where a contract goes
229	
230	A boundary is where the system meets something it does not compile together with itself. At a
231	boundary the contract is the authority and the code is validated against it (constitution,
232	article VI; the decision and its rejected alternatives:
233	[`contracts/README.md`](../../contracts/README.md)).
234	
235	- **`contracts/<kind>/<area>.yaml|.md`** — one file per area, named after the area, **written by
236	  hand and committed**. `openapi/` for HTTP, `asyncapi/` for events, `invariants/` for data
237	  invariants. Every subdirectory carries a `README.md` with a declared compatibility mode; a
238	  directory with no contract declares `**Status:** empty starter` in it, because silence and a
239	  decision look identical in a file tree.
240	- **Never generate a file into this directory.** A copy of a dump has no authority over what it
241	  was copied from; `contracts` (`G20` until the rename) refuses a file with a generator banner, and one shell redirection is
242	  the whole way back to the state this decision reversed.
243	- **The database schema is not here, and that is a decision.** The set of revisions in
244	  `alembic/versions/` is its contract ([`data-model.md`](data-model.md) § Owner of the schema);
245	  the compatibility mode is declared beside the schema, in the same document.
246	- **A machine's output stays output.** `openapi.json` is gitignored and rebuilt on every run;
247	  `./scripts/contracts.sh` compares it against the contract.
248	
249	## Documentation — where a document goes
250	
251	A document that is not normative still has one home, and which home decides who it is written
252	for. Three trees, three readers, and the cut is by **subject** rather than by tone:
253	
254	| Tree | Subject | Reader |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| [`docs/`](../../docs/README.md) | the system: how to set it up, run it, configure it, watch it, back it up and repair it | whoever operates or takes delivery of the application |
257	| [the marketplace's README](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/README.md), and the orchestrator's own document ([`skills/sdd/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/claude-marketplace/blob/main/plugins/forge/skills/sdd/SKILL.md)) | the change process: how a change travels, and the decision table that drives it | whoever runs, ports or alters the process |
258	| [`../rationale/`](../rationale/README.md) | reasoning worth keeping that is not a decision — why a shape was chosen, what was tried, how it broke | whoever changes this in six months |
259	
260	Four rules hold over `docs/`, and each exists because its absence has a named cost:
261	
262	- **Nothing in `docs/` binds.** Where a rule holds, it holds because it stands in `spec/` or
263	  `contracts/`, and the document here **cites the one that owns it**. A descriptive document
264	  read as normative is a second home for one rule, which is the failure
265	  [`../README.md`](../README.md) exists to prevent. Every document therefore carries a
266	  `**For:**` line naming its reader and a `**Normative source:**` line naming what it defers to.
267	- **One subject per file, named after the subject.** `configuration.md`, `monitoring.md` — never
268	  `misc.md`, never a number in the filename. The same rule as § Naming, for the same reason: a
269	  directory that numbers its documents has stopped being able to say what is in them.
270	- **A procedure is a runbook and lives in `docs/runbooks/`.** A runbook says when to use it, the
271	  steps in order, and how you know it worked. A procedure with no last section cannot be
272	  finished by the person who did not write it, which is the person who reads it at three in the
273	  morning.
274	- **Every instruction invokes a script** (the constitution, article XII). A document that tells
275	  somebody to type `terraform apply` has taught them to skip the guard, and the guard is the
276	  point of `scripts/`. The named exception is the AWS CLI, which genuinely is the interface for
277	  the few steps no script wraps.
278	
279	Rejected (decision of 2026-09-06, `cr: historical` — the process manual and the system's
280	documentation were both in `docs/`, and only one of them was there; framework changes are made
281	on the trunk and carry no `delta.md` in which to declare the edit):
282	
283	- **Leave the process manual in `docs/` and give the system's documentation another directory.**
284	  It puts the tree a client reads one directory away from the tree explaining an agent
285	  framework, and names the visitor's directory after the resident. `docs/` is the first place
286	  anybody looks for a manual to the thing the repository builds.
287	- **One directory, two subjects, separated by a naming prefix.** The prefix is a convention a
288	  reader has to learn before the index is legible, and nothing enforces it. The directory
289	  boundary is enforced by the file system.
290	- **Leave `docs/` unwritten and let the operational facts stay where they are** — in
291	  `infra/README.md`, in `CLAUDE.md`, in script headers and in module docstrings. That was the
292	  state this replaces, and its cost is measurable: the rollback semantics lived only in
293	  `scripts/deploy.sh --help`, the log-level convention only in a Python docstring, and no
294	  document anywhere named a restore procedure. Facts that live only where they were written are
295	  facts only their author can find.

297	## Language
298	
299	**The whole repository is written in English.** Prose, identifiers, file names and
300	directory names; `spec/` and `contracts/` along with everything else; the interface, the
301	route paths, the refusal sentences the backend produces, the Gherkin scenarios, the SDD
302	process layer and the scripts. Gate `english` enforces it, and it enforces both halves: the
303	sentences inside a file are judged by counting, and the name of the file is judged by
304	looking it up, because a path has no function words to count.
305	
306	**A number in prose takes a comma as its thousands separator** — `10,000`, never `10 000`.
307	The spaced form is Polish typography that survived the translation in one document while its
308	neighbours used the comma, and a reader should not have to know the repository's history to
309	read a number.
310	
311	**This reverses the decision of 2026-08-31**, which is recorded here rather than deleted.
312	That decision drew the line where a person starts reading a screen: interface copy became
313	English, while route paths, backend refusal sentences, the Gherkin suite and the whole of
314	`spec/` and `contracts/` stayed Polish. Its reasoning was sound at the time — the guestbook
315	screen was rebuilt from a Claude Design mock-up whose sentences are *content*, the routes
316	were already written down and linked, and refusal sentences are backend text that reaches
317	every client rather than one screen. What it produced was a repository with a seam through
318	it: two languages, and a rule for which side of the seam each artefact falls on. The
319	option this reverses to was named and rejected on that day as "English everywhere, routes
320	and refusals included"; the cost it was rejected for — broken links and backend text moving
321	during a frontend change — is a one-off cost that gets larger every month it is deferred,
322	while the seam is a cost paid at every reading.
323	
324	**Rejected, again and for the same reasons as before:** a bilingual tree with translation
325	files (it solves a problem this product does not have and adds a second place for copy to
326	drift from the screen specification — it comes back with a second audience and its own
327	decision); and keeping historical documents in the language they were written in (an audit
328	nobody can read is not a record, and `spec/rationale/` exists to be read). Introducing i18n
329	later still does not require undoing this: English becomes one of the languages, rather
330	than a layer to take off.
331	
332	**What is not translated, and why.** These are not exceptions to the rule; they are things
333	the rule was never about.
334	
335	| What | Stays as it is |
336	|---|---|
337	| parsed keywords — EARS `WHEN`/`SHALL`, delta labels `ADDED`/`MODIFIED`/`REMOVED`, the `**ADR:** none` and `**Verified-by:** manual` markers, front-matter status values | already English, and a contract rather than prose |
338	| stable refusal codes (`guestbook_entry_not_found`) | a contract surface: the code is what a client matches on, and rewording it is a breaking change |
339	| the credential names `e2e/harness/client.py` redacts | a denylist, not prose — dropping a spelling narrows what gets redacted |
340	| non-ASCII text in `golden-set/` | evidence that bytes survive the round trip. **Each half** must carry characters above U+007F; neither need carry any particular language |
341	| a quoted Polish phrase, a proper noun, a historical file name | quotation. `english` has a floor of five lines so that quoting does not read as writing |
342	| `spec/rationale/mockup-guestbook/support.js` | vendored runtime of a design tool, not authored here |

344	**Domain terms keep their source form inside identifiers** (`GuestbookEntry`, `author`), so
345	a field can be grepped from the specification down to the column — see
346	[`../glossary.md`](../glossary.md).

352	- **Python model files**: singular (`models/guestbook_entry.py`); schema, service and router

355	  `useThing.ts`; **libraries**: `camelCase.ts` (`lib/guestbookEntry.ts`).

360

410	## Type safety
411	
412	- **Backend**: full annotations, `Mapped[...]` on every column. Optionality expressed in the
413	  type (`str | None`), not only in the column arguments. `mypy --strict` covers `app`,
414	  `scripts`, `e2e`, `.claude/skills`, `tests/unit` and `tests/fitness`.
415	- **Frontend**: `tsc --noEmit` is part of `build`. API types come from the generated
416	  `src/api/schema.d.ts` — regenerate rather than widen a type.
417	- **The syntax floor is lower than the runtime floor, and deliberately.** `pyproject.toml` pins
418	  `requires-python` to what the application runs on, and `ruff`'s `target-version` to what the
419	  code may be *written* in; the second is the older of the two. The bare-machine scripts start
420	  on whatever `python3` a machine has on PATH rather than on the interpreter `uv` provisions —
421	  `scripts/preflight.py` reporting what is missing, `scripts/ci_summary.py` in the aggregate CI
422	  job, `scripts/app_status.py` behind `status.sh` — and a script that reports a missing Python
423	  cannot ask for one before it parses. `tests/fitness/test_scripts_syntax_floor.py` parses them
424	  at that floor and holds `target-version` to it. The change process holds its own hooks to the
425	  same floor in its own suite, with a `target-version` of its own.
